    GC content of nucleotide sequences

    Source: R/bio-sequence.R
    bio_gc_content.Rd

    Calculates the fraction of G and C among unambiguous bases (A, C, G and T or U). With by_position = TRUE it also returns GC at the first, second and third codon positions (GC1, GC2 and GC3), which are widely used to compare codon usage between genes and genomes.

    Usage

    bio_gc_content(.data, seq = NULL, by_position = FALSE, .into = "gc")

    Arguments

    .data

    A data frame, tibble or bio_seq_tbl().

    seq

    <tidy-select> The sequence column. Can be omitted for a <bio_seq_tbl>.

    by_position

    If TRUE, add gc1, gc2 and gc3 columns as well.

    .into

    Name of the overall GC column.

    Value

    .data with a numeric column .into (and gc1, gc2, gc3 if requested), with values between 0 and 1.

    Examples

    ecoli_cds |>
  bio_gc_content(sequence, by_position = TRUE) |>
  dplyr::group_by(class) |>
  dplyr::summarise(dplyr::across(c(gc, gc3), mean))
#> # A tibble: 2 × 3
#>   class        gc   gc3
#>   <chr>     <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1 other     0.520 0.569
#> 2 ribosomal 0.505 0.490
